   Each current `execute_series` creates a fresh chart. Existing independent
   reports therefore cannot be accumulated by equal endpoints, labels or origin
   values. The future accumulated source history requires an actual shared
   pre-acquisition chart or separately justified original-capture mapping.
2. **Transaction and insufficiency.** One terminal completion is one statistical
   transaction; visit report positions in original order. Successful N1 one/two-
   row `Insufficient` collection commits rows without a fit. Third-or-later
   collection commits only after complete N1/N2 and current-authority success.
   Any quality, conversion, geometry, arithmetic or final-guard refusal preserves
   the prior rows/reference/fit/revision and their original ages. Earlier
   successful transactions in the same report remain committed. Refusal never
   restores a consumed request or grants a threshold-seeking retry.
3. **Capacity and parent.** Select oldest-only replacement for the fitted
   population's existing64-row bound. Stage old rows plus the incoming row,
   remove the oldest in scratch when necessary, then derive one complete N1
   parent and evaluate its suffixes without changing anchors or divisor bits.
   Any later refusal leaves the committed64 untouched. This is a reviewed

   consequence of N1's numeric limit alone. Runs-only auxiliary rows retain
   their separate bounded owner and never enter the fitted-quality population;
   this choice introduces no new auxiliary budget, age threshold or pruning

4. **Publication.** Keep N2's borrowed fit operation-local. Under the canonical
   receiver's exclusive turn, check the exact staged history/revision and actual
   source/configuration/association/clock/mapping ownership, quality/precision
   and scale/calendar revisions, stop/invalidation and original age of every
   retained row. Use trusted monotonic time, reject backwards time and checked
   age/revision overflow, and keep current freshness policy distinct from the
   historical transport deadline. Commit rows, associations, same-fit diagnostics
   and next revision together without an await, callback or unlock after the

  tuple and representation-error bound separately.

  its stated order with separate binary64 operations. Root words are unsigned

  other legal zero results are canonical positive zero. Positive subnormals and

  enclosure or statistical-confidence promise is introduced.

  its explicit maximum; compare `P`, `D−E` and `abs(R)` **inclusively** to their

##### Persistent session API and lifecycle — 8 November 2026

**Reviewed implementation contract; source authoring starts below.** Reuse the
actual checked `SeriesConfig`, `prepare_series` and consuming `execute_series`.
Create an opaque `AcquisitionSession` from an owned immutable configuration and
an engine-created chart before any preparation. Add no dependency, runtime,
mutex, queue, external retire channel or production authority. Existing one-shot
APIs and `TransportFacts::relative_to` retain their contracts.

Selected API shape:

```text
AcquisitionSession::new(SeriesConfig) -> AcquisitionSession
AcquisitionSession::prepare(&mut self)
    -> Result<(PreparedAcquisition<'_>, ControlHandle), AcquisitionError>
PreparedAcquisition::execute(self, &ControlSchedule)
    -> Result<AcquisitionReport, AcquisitionError>
AcquisitionSession::retire(&mut self)
AcquisitionReport::series(&self) -> &SeriesReport
AcquisitionReport::chart_origin(&self) -> Instant
AcquisitionReport::same_session(&self, &Self) -> bool
```

The prepared guard holds an exclusive mutable session borrow and the actual
private prepared plan; execution retains that borrow through the existing
driver's timer/runtime cleanup. Only that operation can construct a report
wrapper, from its genuine returned series and the chart captured before its
preparation. No public operation accepts a caller-paired report, facts/context
tuple or chart. The immutable report retains metadata only; matching provenance
is not current authority. The session retains no report collection. Private
identity, checked configuration reuse and owning construction enforce these
invariants; no new raw scalar admission or second validation rule is introduced.

| State/action | Required result and effect |
| --- | --- |
| Idle, successful prepare | One Prepared guard; no socket/runtime; existing entropy/token admission is unchanged. |
| Idle, failed prepare | Original typed driver refusal; remain Idle; no hidden retry. |
| Prepared guard dropped unused | Drop the actual prepared resources before returning the session to Idle. |
| Prepared guard deliberately forgotten | Remain Busy; another prepare refuses before entropy/native work. |
| Execute consumes guard | Transition to Executing before invoking the driver; no second preparation or quiescent retirement is expressible while its exclusive borrow is held. |
| Driver returns clean Completed, Stopped or SeriesDeadline | Return the original report with pre-acquisition chart metadata; return to Idle only after cleanup. |
| Driver returns Stale/Failure or any primary/cleanup failure | Retain the original report and retire the session. |
| Driver returns an outer error or encounters a structural contradiction | Retire the session; preserve the actual typed error; never reopen capacity as if execution completed normally. |
| Unexpected unwind | Drop marks the session Retired and the original unwind propagates; add no production panic catcher or fabricated typed failure. |
| Quiescent retire | Idempotently select terminal Retired, including a forgotten-plan Busy state; all later preparations refuse. |
| Configuration/association replacement | Retire/drop the old quiescent owner and create a fresh session/chart; no in-place mutation or old-handle retargeting. |

Retirement is explicitly quiescent. Active interruption uses the original plan's
`ControlHandle`; the caller waits for actual execution/cleanup before retirement
or replacement. A stop request is delivery, not completion. Normal report
classification preserves the qualified historical-transfer/fresh-summary cutoff;
no wrapper can erase a historical completion or renew its age. Unknown Windows
native completion remains unqualified under the existing execution hold.

### N3a finite same-source acquisition and completion receiver contract

**Independently reviewed READY for finite source implementation, 7 November
2026.** This is the first admitted acquisition/receiver child after N2, within
the existing observation-to-Core chain. Production sample/history admission and
all native execution holds remain separate.
Owner: engine/protocol/QA, with S1.2 retaining later numerical/history admission.
Requirements: REQ-8/BND-1 and CHECK-6/7/8/11/14/25/27. Environment: admitted Linux,
controlled loopback UDP only; no Windows, formal, public network or clock effects.

**Observable source exit.** One engine-owned series makes exactly three planned
sequential attempts to one explicitly configured loopback endpoint and moves
each terminal completion once into bounded private receiving state. Three is a
fixed attempt count, not a target of three successful measurements or permission
to retry failed requests. The report distinguishes completed transport facts,
nominal measurement refusal/unavailability and attempts not started because of
terminal control/deadline/setup failure. Statistical admission is explicitly
unavailable and admitted/eligible sample count remains zero.

**Actual owners and API.** Add a small `series` owner in `nevrotick-engine`, with
minimal `lib.rs` orchestration/reuse changes and focused private/public tests.
Reuse actual `LiveSlot`, staging/commit/retirement, `measurement.rs` and
`relative.rs`; add no Cargo dependency, generic runtime framework or N1/N2 input
adapter. Keep the existing two-distinct-peer API and its one-query contract.
The additive checked surface is `SeriesConfig::new(peer, request_timeout,
series_timeout)`, optional already-checked experimental profile attachment,
`prepare_series(&SeriesConfig)` and consuming
`execute_series(PreparedSeries, &ControlSchedule)`. Config/prepared/report fields
remain private, without raw/default/deserialization/mutation bypasses. A sole
fallible constructor invokes adopted Garde rules for new raw configuration and
token candidates. Source/exchange identity is created by actual preparation and
execution, never accepted as matching caller labels.

**Preparation and bounds.** Accept the existing loopback/nonzero-port/address
scope rules. Both durations are positive, at most the existing laboratory
`MAX_TIMEOUT` (30s), and request timeout cannot exceed series timeout. Preparation
reads one24-byte entropy buffer for three distinct nonzero eight-byte tokens,
rejecting zero/duplicate tokens without entropy retry or send. It creates no
socket queue. Execution uses one private current-thread runtime and at most one
active socket/request, one49-byte receive buffer and three owned terminal records.
Bind/register a fresh request socket sequentially; record setup failure as a
terminal series cause rather than silently replacing/retrying it. All remaining
planned attempts then remain explicitly not started. Each request allows at most
the existing64 readiness-driven send attempts and64 selected native datagrams,
with one confirmed query send and no retransmission. Whole-series limits are
192 such send attempts,192 selected datagrams and three confirmed sends.

**Time and identity.** Capture one actual `Instant` origin before runtime/native
setup. Total deadline is checked `origin + series_timeout`; each actual request
has checked `min(request_start + request_timeout, total_deadline)`. Later setup,
waiting or reevaluation never resets the total deadline. Each request has a fresh
actual request/socket owner, its prepared unique correlation token and the same
immutable configured-source/series context. Reports retain that shared context
and the actual `TransportFacts`, without native handles. New series have distinct
contexts even at the same address. Do not rearm a `Done` slot or call the old
two-peer `execute` repeatedly and relabel its distinct origins as one series.
This limited source/configuration identity establishes neither authenticated
server identity nor independent votes, production clock/mapping generations or
calibrated UTC accuracy. Existing aggregate control epoch remains laboratory
control, not a substitute for those unavailable production suppliers.

**State and completion.** The exclusive owner checks latest stop/invalidation,
deadline and request state before send, after selected I/O, and again immediately
before reply commit. Completion transfer is a private move from the actual
terminal request into the matching series/request position, checked against
actual owner identity and current control epoch. Duplicate/cross-series/stale
transfer cannot overwrite prior records or revive a request. Correlated
ordinary-header completion consumes its request even when nominal measurement
is refused. Preserve that irreversible retirement independently of downstream
numerical acceptance: rejection preserves earlier observation/history payloads
but never restores `Pending`. Malformed or wrong-origin datagrams consume the
bounded receive budget and may precede a valid neighboring reply; they do not
become completed measurements. Stop, invalidation or total deadline retires the
active request and marks later attempts not started, without extra sends.

**Historical meaning and cleanup.** Preserve real capture brackets, acquisition
and processing times, endpoints, raw signed RTT, corrected rational phase and
the exact half-nanosecond midpoint representation. Retain original acquisition
age; comparing views or choosing another anchor never makes an old result fresh.
Keep original date/model declarations and typed measurement refusal. No raw
clock reading, LI=0, host date or consistency tolerance supplies true-date/scale,
calendar, capture/mapping bound, quantum, prior frequency interval, quality
distance or unit weight. Those suppliers, NTS, statistical uncertainty/expiry/

private transaction problem identified above, not copied N2 scalar certificates.
Retire/drop the current socket before preparing the next; reap any owned stop/
invalidation timers and drop the runtime before return, preserving cleanup errors
alongside a primary failure. Rust drop/host completion is not native Windows

**Independent acceptance and finite execution.** Through the real loopback entry,
observe three requests to the same destination, pairwise distinct actual exchange
identities/tokens, one common-origin reconstruction and no fourth send. Challenge
an old reply replayed at the next socket, malformed-then-valid neighboring replies,

###### Engine receive chronology at policy, commit and recovery boundaries

This W11-W01/S2.2 continuation addresses TQ-01/09, REQ-8, BND-2, AC-04 and
CHECK-6/8/9/11/21/25/27. It starts from staged tree `b07eb782603fd7eafbd821c24c80603b2947bb32`
and product `978691a8`. The staged source and unchanged dependency configuration
carry the original clocks, ownership and deadlines into the three owners.

- **Managed plain KoD.** The policy owner checks the actual reserved send
  observation against the start of the original receive bracket before either
  restriction record changes. A selected reply whose receive starts before
  the reserved send charges one rejection and leaves the same request pending.
  The same query can accept at exact send/arrival equality. The request deadline,
  source and endpoint binding, and admitted floors retain their original meaning.
- **Retired ordinary protected commit.** Under current Control and source
  policy, the final observation cannot precede the authenticated receipt's
  acceptance reading. It remains strictly before the original expiry. The
  guard covers terminal cookie publication and the private first-request
  continuation. Refusal retains the original charged work and historical
  receipt and leaves the cookie pools intact. Stop, currentness and deadline
  retain their existing precedence; a committed result keeps its history.
- **Final authenticated count refusal.** Recovery retirement checks both
  original receive readings with the same span check used by ordinary
  admission. A reversed bracket gives the retirement cause `Time`; an upper
  reading at the original cutoff gives `Deadline`. Both preserve the
  initiating `Cookies` failure and the original debit, retire the actual
  backend, and grant no retry draw or successor. Ordered exhaustion can
  still defer one bounded replacement, and a healthy final packet can commit
  in the original context.

###### Automatic resume invalidation in the Windows observe CLI

This W11-W02/S2.1 source child routes the automatic-resume event to the
actual plain observe invocation under TQ-07/09 and CHECK-11/21/25/27.
After preparing its sockets, the CLI subscribes before emitting bound
records or executing the pilot. The safe subscription accepts one action,
which delivers invalidation through the invocation's existing
`ControlHandle`. An unrelated event leaves the action pending. Automatic
resume consumes it once. The existing owner guards decide whether pending
work can publish. A completed result keeps its historical facts.

The dependency-free `windows-platform-native` leaf owns the two PowrProf
calls. Engine and the existing portable platform crate retain
`forbid(unsafe_code)`, as does the leaf's portable callback state module.
The new FFI leaf uses `deny(unsafe_code)` and three item-local
`expect(unsafe_code)` attributes covering the import block and the two
documented calls. Callback storage lasts for the process and cannot be
rebound. Close disarms delivery before attempting native unregistration,
with no slot lock held across that call. Removed captures remain owned until
the unregistration attempt finishes. The CLI preserves an earlier error and
reports cleanup failure separately. Registration failure refuses the run
before any bound row or packet is emitted. The native adapter is a Windows-only
Engine dependency under both default and EP1.

cleanup refusal. The managed failure report could therefore repeat an
original source-policy, deadline or native transport failure.

Establishment now inspects the existing latch before attempting close.
A preparation failure that already reports that latch keeps only its
primary cause. A typed TLS primary can still retain a separate failure
observed while attempting the TLS alert. When no earlier fault blocked close,
the actual close operation still contributes its own result. A newly observed
close refusal still blocks candidate publication. The stream retires before
the single decision to return a failure or hand off the association.

observed worker and joined report. A bounded loopback peer reads the
`ClientHello`, waits for native read admission, replaces the original
configuration with equal values at a new revision and releases the read.

duplicate cleanup, no retained association or UDP, peer EOF and joined
worker and observer retirement. The notification is immediately before
the socket read. The case targets replacement between read admission
and the post-read guard. Replacing a source during a confirmed blocked syscall
and faulting the close-notify drain remain separate observations. An external
wall bound owns the test process.

##### Request cancellation from the retired Windows DNS worker

W11-W03 DNS-3, THR-26 and CHECK-25/27. Explicit retirement and Drop now reach
the same dispatch's atomic state. A retirement that wins before dispatch
prevents submission. After dispatch, the worker observes retirement while

pending query, then waits for completion without further polling. Callback
cleanup and any in-flight cancellation retain the provider allocation and
permit. The Engine slot still requires actual Windows thread exit and join.

completed but unread result therefore leaves no extra native permit owner.

cancellation can still race callback invocation. Microsoft’s sample uses
that overlap while retaining the shared context, then waits for the callback.
The result and cancellation status remain separate. Neither cancellation
status changes the retired round’s report or allows a second query.
